collection_name: Deltadalen Member, Vikinghøgda Formation, Svalbard Lower Triassic
geogcomments:
The dominant sediment supply from the west resulted in extensive deposits of coastal and shallow marine sandstones and shales in western Spitsbergen, whereas shales with minor siltstones and sandstones were deposited in a basinal setting in central and eastern Spitzbergen, Barentsøya and Edgeøya. This sedimentary pattern continues southwards under the Barents Sea, with deposition of shales in basins and courser grained clastics along the basin margins and on local highs.
The complete member is exposed in Deltadalen, Lusitaniadalen (western side of Vikinghøgda) and on the flank of the southern hill of Stensiöfjellet at its transition to Sassendalen. The upper part of the member is exposed in several sections in the outcrop area of the unit, and a more condensed development (without the earliest Triassic beds occur at Barensøya and Edgeøya. The uppermost part of the Kapp Starostin Formation and the basal sandstone of the Deltadalen Member forms a cliff exposed on both sides of the Deltadalen River.
The base of the Deltadalen Member is defined at the weathering surface of the Kapp Storastin Formation
lithdescript:
68 meters thick
Lower part of the Deltadalen member: sandstone and siltstone interbeds are abundant.
Calcite concretions are the most abundant in the upper part of the Lusitaniadalen Member but do also occur in the Deltadalen member, but with different carbonate mineralogy.
The basal sandstone of the Deltadalen member consits of 2-3 meter of medium to fine grained glauconitic grey-green sandstone, that occasionally shows faint cross bedding.
The sandstone is moderately bioturbated and has a patchly chert cement
Above the basal sandstone, the Deltadalen Member consits of silty shale with intervals dominated by siltstone or very fine grained sandstone beds.
Several intervals enriched in sandy siltstone beds occur throughout the member, and several show hummockly lamination, the upper part parts of which are often rippled. Bioturbation is sparse.
The top of the member consits of thin sandstone beds forming an upward-coarsing upward sequence.
geology_comments:
Deltaic coast
Transgressive due to the transgressive sandstone bed, which also indicates rapid establishment of conditions favourable for bentic colonization.
The repeated occurrences of siltstone and sandstone beds with hummockly lamination indicates a storm influence on a shelf above storm wave base.
preservation_comments: Macrofossils which can be identified are restricted almost exclusively to concretions. Shales between the fossiliferous concretion-levels are either not fossiliferous or have only indeterminate fauna so detailed ammonoid zones or distinctive biostratigraphical boundaries, cannot easily be defined. The fauna of a single concretionlayer represents a snapshot of the zone or higher biostratigraphical unit, consequently only comparison with ammonoid assemblages from other more fossiliferous boreal Triassic successions, such as Siberia and the Canadian Artic.

collection_name: Vendomdalen Member, Vikinghøgda Formation, Svalbard Lower Triassic
geogcomments:
The lower and Middle Triassic succession of Svalbard consists of fine-grained clastics. The dominant sediment supply from the west resulted in extensive deposits of coastal and shallow marine sandstones and shales in western Spitsbergen, whereas shales with minor siltstones and sandstones were deposited in a basinal setting in central and eastern Spitzbergen, Barentsøya and Edgeøya. This sedimentary pattern continues southwards under the Barents Sea, with deposition of shales in basins and courser grained clastics along the basin margins and on local highs.
Well exposed in a valley 15 km south-east of Vikinghøgda in the surrounding mountain sides. The lower part of the type section is defined at the southern foot of Vikinghøgda, where the basal beds are well exposed. The major part of the member ( and the upper boundary ) is exposed in all outcropping areas of the Vikinghøgda formation. The type section ( except the basal beds ) is defined on the eastern slope of Vikinghøgda.
Ca. 1.5 km north-east where exposures from the bivalve bed ( at 173 m) upwards occur at ridges between melt water creeks, the part of the member, which is not exposed in the valley 15 km south-east of Vikinghøgda, is found.
lithdescript:
94 meters thick
Dolomite beds and nodules are common, with a few silty interbeds.
Calcite concretions are the most abundant in the upper part of the Lusitaniadalen Member but do also occur in the Vendomdalen member, but with different carbonate mineralogy.
18 meters above the base of the member a prominent bivalve-rich dolomite bed is present which can be correlates the two sections.
The member consits of silty, dark grey laminated mudstone, thin- to medium-bedded with more or less silty, yellow weathering, dolomite beds and nodules. A clear shift from grey to dark gery mudstone takes place at the lower bouderay, and the yellow weathering dolomite beds are distinctive of the Vendomdalen Member throughout central Spitzbergen. The dolomitic beds may be up to 1.5 meters thick, but most are 10-30 cm thick. Dolomitic nodules, some of them septarian, are up to tens of centimetres in diameter, flattened nodules may reach several metres in horizontal extent, but generally only 0.5 m in thickness. Rare calcite concretions occur near the top of the member.
From the bivalve bed, that occurs upward at ridges of several meltwater creeks, the section consists of several 3 to 12 m thick, faintly coarsening upward units, grading from laminated shale to silty mudstone, capped with dolomite beds, sometimes silty or sandy, or consisting of dolomite lenses. The dolomite beds consits of sucrose, ferrous dolomite and were formed relatively late in diagenesis. The upper 50 m consists of plana laminated silty grey mudstone with thin dolomite beds. At the top is a pronounced silty/sandy dolomite bed. The bed shows some ripple lamination.
Above the top bed, very dark grey shale with small phosphate nodules is referred to the Botheheia Formation. Seven metres above the base of the Botheheia Formation there is a dolomitic siltstone bed, which represents a local marker in the lowermost part of this formation in the Sassendalen area.
geology_comments: The member represents distal shelf deposits, below wave base, with accumulation of marine derived organic material in a low oxic environment.

geogcomments: Jameson Land, East Greenland.\r\nComplete P-Tr section with both an abundant marine flora (and fauna) and a well-preseved terrestrial palynomorph record. The exposures of Permian-Triassic marine outcrop along East Greenland between 71 and 75º North correspond to the upper part of the Schuchert Dal Formation and the overlying Wordie Creek Formation.\r\n
stratcomments: The locality shows a transition from the upper Oksedal Member of the Schuchert Dal Formation into the base of the overlying Wordie Creek Formation.
lithdescript:
The earliest Triassic in particular was a time of active rifting and rapid subsidence that resulted in an exceedingly thick marine succession. Some 700 m of predominantly silicalstic sediment were deposited during this interval and comprise the Wordie Creek Formation.
The Greenland P-Tr record is among the most expanded in the world.
This area is far enough away from later igneous intrusions that it has suffered no thermal alternation, unlike other localities elsewere.
geology_comments: The sediments of the Schuchert Dal Formation and the overlying Wordie Creek Formation were deposited in a narrow, elongate, fault controlled basin. A well oxygenated benthic environment.

stratcomments: Most recently, the Thaynes formation has been separated into four facies belts, which include a basinal facies, an outer shelf facies, an inner shelf facies, and a red bed facies. the basinal facies consists of dark grey to black very siltly lime mudstones and gray to loive drab siltstones and shales. The outer shelf facies belt is characterized by dark grayish brown whole fossil wackestone, ranging to light gray bioclastic grainstone, with minor interbedded sanstone, siltstone, and mudstone. The inner shelf facies includes a variety of lithologies, mainly fine-grained mudstone and silty limestone, along with less common dolomite, siltstone, and bioturbated mudstone.

stratcomments: Most recently, the Thaynes formation has been separated into four facies belts, which include a basinal facies, an outer shelf facies, an inner shelf facies, and a red bed facies. the basinal facies consists of dark grey to black very siltly lime mudstones and gray to loive drab siltstones and shales. The outer shelf facies belt is characterized by dark grayish brown whole fossil wackestone, ranging to light gray bioclastic grainstone, with minor interbedded sanstone, siltstone, and mudstone. The inner shelf facies includes a variety of lithologies, mainly fine-grained mudstone and silty limestone, along with less common dolomite, siltstone, and bioturbated mudstone.

stratcomments: The Moenkopi Formation in southwestern Utah contains three limestone members. The lower limestone member, the Timpoweap is only very sparsely fossiliferous and is primarily a marginal marine deposit. The middle limestone, the Virgin Member, contains limestone units deposited under normal marine conditions during the Spathian trangression. The upper limestone, the Schnabkaib Limestone, is unfossiliferous and mainly evaporitic. These limestone members are separated by red members, informally distinguished as lower, middle, and upper.

stratcomments: The Moenkopi Formation in southwestern Utah contains three limestone members. The lower limestone member, the Timpoweap is only very sparsely fossiliferous and is primarily a marginal marine deposit. The middle limestone, the Virgin Member, contains limestone units deposited under normal marine conditions during the Spathian trangression. The upper limestone, the Schnabkaib Limestone, is unfossiliferous and mainly evaporitic. These limestone members are separated by red members, informally distinguished as lower, middle, and upper.

geogcomments: Capitol Reef, Grand wash: Sec. 35, T.29S, R.6E
stratcomments: The Moenkopi Formation in southwestern Utah contains three limestone members. The lower limestone member, the Timpoweap is only very sparsely fossiliferous and is primarily a marginal marine deposit. The middle limestone, the Virgin Member, contains limestone units deposited under normal marine conditions during the Spathian trangression. The upper limestone, the Schnabkaib Limestone, is unfossiliferous and mainly evaporitic. These limestone members are separated by red members, informally distinguished as lower, middle, and upper.
lithdescript: Low-relief shell banks or amalgamanted shell beds, subject to wave action. These massive bioclastic packstones are dominated by nested large bivalves and bivalves fragments, held in a micritic matrix without any preferenial orientation.

geogcomments: Hidden Pasture Springs: sec. 23, T.13S, R.10W, Beaverhead County
stratcomments: The Dinwoody ranges in thickness from just a few meters in the east to about 270m in the southwest. Previous studies suggesting stratigraphic subdivision of the Dinwoody based on lithologic or paleontologic criteria have been discredited. Dominance of a basinal conodont fauna suggests that a broad relatively quiet marine embayment prevailed throughout much of the Early Triassic. The Dinwoody consists of olive-gray shale and siltstone with linestone interbeds that increase in frequency and thickness up section. Interbedded limestones and minor amounts of dolomites are dominated by bioclastic wackestones and packstones.

Hidden Pasture Springs: sec. 23, T.13S, R.10W, Beaverhead County
stratcomments: The Dinwoody ranges in thickness from just a few meters in the east to about 270m in the southwest. Previous studies suggesting stratigraphic subdivision of the Dinwoody based on lithologic or paleontologic criteria have been discredited. Dominance of a basinal conodont fauna suggests that a broad relatively quiet marine embayment prevailed throughout much of the Early Triassic. The Dinwoody consists of olive-gray shale and siltstone with linestone interbeds that increase in frequency and thickness up section. Interbedded limestones and minor amounts of dolomites are dominated by bioclastic wackestones and packstones.
lithdescript: Wave-influenced bioclastic packstones

geogcomments: The Strzelc Opolskie Quarry provides one of the best exposures of the Muschelkalk deposits in Upper Silesia. Paleogeographically, this is the southern margin of the Germanic basin. The Muschelkalk Sea was connected with the Tethys Ocean to the south.
stratcomments: Middle Triassic/Lower Muschelkalk: The paleoecologic analysis is based on five sections from the Strzelc Opolskie Quarry. The five sections cover the entire span of the Terebratula Beds and the lowermost part of the Karchowice Beds. The Terebratula Beds are subdivided into three units: Lower marls, Crinoid limestones, and Coquina and wavy limestones (See lithological description below for details) Upper Silesian Region
lithdescript:
Lower marls - Crumpled and wavy limestones dominate in this unit. Shelly fossils are practically absent. Only in one place badly preserved tiny bivalves have been observed. 
Crinoid Limestone - Two firmgrounds occur in the lower part of this unit. the middle and upper parts are composed of thick calcarenitic beds. Dominant skeletal components change upward from mixed skeletal debris in the lower part, through crinoid columnals in the middle part, to terebratulid shell debis in the upper part. 
Coquinas and wavy limestone - Four lithological types have been distinguished: 
a) brachiopod coqunia. Up to 30 cm thick coquina layers, separated by crumpled and wavy limestone, occur in the whole unit. 
b) Crumpled and wavy limestone. Limestone beds which exhibit deformational structures varying from wavy bedding and gentle undulation, to structures intricately crumpled and fragmented. Fossils uncommon but their number increase upward.
c) Bivalve coquina. This lithology appears in the uppermost part if the unit as thin shell beds composed of closely packed internal molds of small articulated bivalves.
d) Organodetrial limestone with foraminifers. Numerous benthic forams are the main component of this limestone. 
Karchowice Beds - Crinoid and micritic limestones dominate in this unit. Sponges as well as brachiopods are identified. Very numerous are columnals of crinoids and in places, shells of unidentified bivalves. Hardgrounds with a rich assemblages of trace fossiles are well developed on the micritic limestone bedding planes

d) Organodetrial limestone with foraminifers. Numerous benthic forams are the main component of this limestone. 
Karchowice Beds - Crinoid and micritic limestones dominate in this unit. Sponges as well as brachiopods are identified. Very numerous are columnals of crinoids and in places, shells of unidentified bivalves. Hardgrounds with a rich assemblages of trace fossiles are well developed on the micritic limestone bedding planes

stratcomments: Most recently, the Thaynes formation has been separated into four facies belts, which include a basinal facies, an outer shelf facies, an inner shelf facies, and a red bed facies. the basinal facies consists of dark grey to black very siltly lime mudstones and gray to loive drab siltstones and shales. The outer shelf facies belt is characterized by dark grayish brown whole fossil wackestone, ranging to light gray bioclastic grainstone, with minor interbedded sanstone, siltstone, and mudstone. The inner shelf facies includes a variety of lithologies, mainly fine-grained mudstone and silty limestone, along with less common dolomite, siltstone, and bioturbated mudstone.

stratcomments: 8 feet above base of CCR section.\r\nGerster Formation is correlated with the upper Phosphoria Formation (Rex Chert, Retort, Tosi) and other upper units in the Park City Group (Franson, Ervay). Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

stratcomments: 363 feet above base of measured section.\r\nGerster Formation is correlated with the upper Phosphoria Formation (Rex Chert, Retort, Tosi) and other upper units in the Park City Group (Franson, Ervay). Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

stratcomments: 675 feet above base of measured section.\r\nGerster Formation is correlated with the upper Phosphoria Formation (Rex Chert, Retort, Tosi) and other upper units in the Park City Group (Franson, Ervay). Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

stratcomments: 962 feet above base of measured section.\r\nGerster Formation is correlated with the upper Phosphoria Formation (Rex Chert, Retort, Tosi) and other upper units in the Park City Group (Franson, Ervay). Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

stratcomments: 41 feet above base of measured section\r\nGerster Formation is correlated with the upper Phosphoria Formation (Rex Chert, Retort, Tosi) and other upper units in the Park City Group (Franson, Ervay). Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

stratcomments: 765 feet above base of Gerster Formation.\r\nGerster Formation is correlated with the upper Phosphoria Formation (Rex Chert, Retort, Tosi) and other upper units in the Park City Group (Franson, Ervay). Those units are now Lopingian in age, following a latest Capitanian U/Pb age of 260.57 Ma in the upper Meade Peak Member. The upper age of the Gerster is unclear, and it may span much of the Lopingian, although the top is unconformable (overlying units are Smithian) so some or all of the Changhsingian may be missing. For now, all collections are assigned a Wuchiapingian age.

(f) Calcarenite, crinoid debris, upper beds cross laminated; grades abruptly to east into bed 28.

geogcomments: The Anisian Leidapo Member of the Qinguan Formation is exposed in the Qingyan area, about 30 km south of Guiyang (provincial capital), Guizhou Province, China
stratcomments: The Qingyan Formation is composed of limestones and mudstones and is about 800m thick. In ascending order, it is subdivided into the Xiaoshan, Mafengpo, Yingshangpo, Leidapo, and Yuqing members. According to palaeontological data, the latter two members are assigned to the upper Anisian, whereas the other three are regarded as lower Anisian in age.
lithdescript: The Leidpo Member discussed in this paper, occupying the lower part of the upper Anisian, is about 200m thick and consists of mudstones, shales and marls. this member is characterized by fossiliferous mudstones and marls. It is grouped into three parts. The lower and upper parts are mainly composed of massive. laminated mudstone with abundant "paper shelled bivalves". The middle part consists of alternating beds of mudstone and marl.
geology_comments: The Qingyan Formation is present in the northern part of the Middle Triassic Nanpanjiang Basin (or the Dian-Qian-Gui Basin), which was filled mainly with carbonate platform, bank and siliciclastic basinal deposits. the shallow-water carbonate platform is called the Yangtze Platform and was a stable palaeogeographic element from the Late Proterozoic to the Triassic.

In ascending order, it is subdivided into the Xiaoshan, Mafengpo, Yingshangpo, Leidapo, and Yuqing members. According to palaeontological data, the latter two members are assigned to the upper Anisian, whereas the other three are regarded as lower Anisian in age.
lithdescript: The Leidpo Member discussed in this paper, occupying the lower part of the upper Anisian, is about 200m thick and consists of mudstones, shales and marls. this member is characterized by fossiliferous mudstones and marls. It is grouped into three parts. The lower and upper parts are mainly composed of massive. laminated mudstone with abundant "paper shelled bivalves". The middle part consists of alternating beds of mudstone and marl.\r\n\r\nThe Qingyan Formation is present in the northern part of the Middle Triassic Nanpanjiang Basin (or the Dian-Qian-Gui Basin), which was filled mainly with carbonate platform, bank and siliciclastic basinal deposits. the shallow-water carbonate platform is called the Yangtze Platform and was a stable palaeogeographic element from the Late Proterozoic to the Triassic.

lithdescript: Lower member is composed of muddy siltstone, and shale, and minor brown sandstone.
preservation_comments: Most of the brachiopods are represented by isolated valves and are poorly preserved with worn surfaces indicating that the shells were abraded during transportation prior to deposition.

geogcomments: The Anisian Leidapo Member of the Qinguan Formation is exposed in the Qingyan area, about 30 km south of Guiyang (provincial capital), Guizhou Province, China
stratcomments: The Qingyan Formation is composed of limestones and mudstones and is about 800m thick. In ascending order, it is subdivided into the Xiaoshan, Mafengpo, Yingshangpo, Leidapo, and Yuqing members. According to palaeontological data, the latter two members are assigned to the upper Anisian, whereas the other three are regarded as lower Anisian in age.
lithdescript: The Leidpo Member discussed in this paper, occupying the lower part of the upper Anisian, is about 200m thick and consists of mudstones, shales and marls. this member is characterized by fossiliferous mudstones and marls. It is grouped into three parts. The lower and upper parts are mainly composed of massive. laminated mudstone with abundant "paper shelled bivalves". The middle part consists of alternating beds of mudstone and marl.\r\n\r\nThe Qingyan Formation is present in the northern part of the Middle Triassic Nanpanjiang Basin (or the Dian-Qian-Gui Basin), which was filled mainly with carbonate platform, bank and siliciclastic basinal deposits. the shallow-water carbonate platform is called the Yangtze Platform and was a stable palaeogeographic element from the Late Proterozoic to the Triassic.

The middle part consists of alternating beds of mudstone and marl.\r\n\r\nThe Qingyan Formation is present in the northern part of the Middle Triassic Nanpanjiang Basin (or the Dian-Qian-Gui Basin), which was filled mainly with carbonate platform, bank and siliciclastic basinal deposits. the shallow-water carbonate platform is called the Yangtze Platform and was a stable palaeogeographic element from the Late Proterozoic to the Triassic.

According to palaeontological data, the latter two members are assigned to the upper Anisian, whereas the other three are regarded as lower Anisian in age.
lithdescript: The Leidpo Member discussed in this paper, occupying the lower part of the upper Anisian, is about 200m thick and consists of mudstones, shales and marls. this member is characterized by fossiliferous mudstones and marls. It is grouped into three parts. The lower and upper parts are mainly composed of massive. laminated mudstone with abundant "paper shelled bivalves". The middle part consists of alternating beds of mudstone and marl.\r\n\r\nThe Qingyan Formation is present in the northern part of the Middle Triassic Nanpanjiang Basin (or the Dian-Qian-Gui Basin), which was filled mainly with carbonate platform, bank and siliciclastic basinal deposits. the shallow-water carbonate platform is called the Yangtze Platform and was a stable palaeogeographic element from the Late Proterozoic to the Triassic.

collection_name: Non-brachiopod fauna, Gua Musang Formation, Merapoh, Pahang
geogcomments: Road and rail cuts 10-20 km south of Merapoh along Dada Kering-Gua Musang highway. Rail cuts NE of Sungai Temau Station.
stratcomments: Listed as lower and middle Changhsingian (Oldhamina dicipens and Haydenella minuta [local?] zones, respectively), but more likely Capitanian.
lithdescript: Argillaceous lithofacies is dominated by thinly bedded to massive shales and mudstones, interbedded with minor tuffaceous siltstones, sandstones, or pebbly sandstone layers and locally with thin limestone lenses. Slightly metamorphosed and deformed locally.
preservation_comments: Mostly preserved as moulds and casts with traces of iron oxide in some of the fresh specimens. Some pyritized and calcified shells were also found. Brachiopod spines are usually well preserved and the brachiopod and bivalve valves are very commonly preserved intact, suggesting the fauna has undergone very little transportation.
collection_comments: Bivalves are dominant at MSY14.
taxonomy_comments: Includes bivalves, gastropods, cephalopods, bryozoans, corals, trilobites, crinoids, algae, sponges, and fusulinids that are not included in the brachiopod faunal lists MSY1-18.

stratcomments: Age originally given as Changhsingian but more likely Capitanian (Campi et al. 2005)
lithdescript: Argillaceous lithofacies is dominated by thinly bedded to massive shales and mudstones, interbedded with minor tuffaceous siltstones, sandstones, or pebbly sandstone layers and locally with thin limestone lenses. Slightly metamorphosed and deformed locally.
preservation_comments: Mostly preserved as moulds and casts with traces of iron oxide in some of the fresh specimens. Some pyritized and calcified shells were also found. Brachiopod spines are usually well preserved and the brachiopod and bivalve valves are very commonly preserved intact, suggesting the fauna has undergone very little transportation.

geogcomments: Location stated as 99.60' W, 18 degrees 80'N, shown more accurately on map in Ishibashi et al. 1994. North and east of Chiangmai, on or near the Lampang-Ngao road, south of Ngao.
stratcomments: Huai Tak Formation is uppermost of Ngao Group, overlain by latest Permian volcanics and Triassic Lampang Group.
preservation_comments: Moderately well preserved, chiefly as natural moulds, but are deformed and so crowded together that it is impossible to avoid some breakage in extracting specimens. A number of species are represented by fragments.
taxonomy_comments: Only includes brachiopods. Fusilinids and conodonts are absent, as are corals, gastropods, and bryozoans. A number of pteriiform and myalinid bivalves and rare ammonoid impressions are present.

collection_name: W1333, Section 18, Nangung Khola, Karnali (Nangung Fm)
geogcomments: Upstream of junction of Nangung Khola (River) and Panjang Khola.
stratcomments: Nangung Formation is correlated with the Kalabagh Member of the Salt Range based on brachiopods, which is Wuchiapingian in age. 12 m thick.
lithdescript: Quartzite.
preservation_comments: Found principally as shells, and sometimes as weathered casts. No material has been silicified and much of it has been distorted under mountain building stress. Preservation is, on the whole, not very favourable.
collection_comments: Some collections were of individual specimens, others as large as possible under the circumstances, with a few localities represented by rock weighing more than 50 kg. Most collections were made from just over 50 measured sections, and are under good stratigraphic control.
lithdescript.1: Quartzite.

geogcomments: The fossiliferous outcrops on the Oreg Hill near Vaszoly were discovered by I. Szabo and the first detailed collection made by the Hungarian Geological Survey was led also by him. The investigated section is located between Vaszoly and Pecsely villages and the Lake Balaton, on the gentle eastern slope of the Oreg Hill. 3 metres wide and 10 metres long trench, directed to SW–NE direction, was excavated in more than two metres depth, near the top of the Öreg Hill, in a grassy belt between two wooded areas (coordinates: x=46°55'45", y=17° 47'05").
stratcomments: Camunum subzone. Newly exposed trench reveals a sequence of about 6m in thickness, belonging to the Dorgicse Formation (somewhat equivalent of the formerly used "Buchenstein Beds" overlying the Anisian Megyehegy Dolomite Formation).

geogcomments: Section measured from Yinshangpo to Sizishan, in the vicinity of Qingyan, a small town 25 km S of Guiyang, the capital of Guizhou Province.
stratcomments: Bed 4 (units KC 259-262) is 80 m thick. About 200 m above base of Qingyan Formation.
lithdescript: Qingyan Formation consists mainly of gray to yellowish-green noncalcareous shale, pale-to dark-gray marl, calcareous shale, and argillaceous limestone, usually thin-bedded. Most of the fossils are collected from the shale and marl.
geology_comments: Evaporative basin in Sichuan and north Guizhou separated from open marine to south in Yunnan and Guangxi by biohermal belt, located just north of Qingyan. The area near Qingyan was a prebiohermal facies. (Apparently fore-reef or something equivalent, located on the slope?)

lithdescript: Qingyan Formation consists mainly of gray to yellowish-green noncalcareous shale, pale-to dark-gray marl, calcareous shale, and argillaceous limestone, usually thin-bedded. Most of the fossils are collected from the shale and marl.

geogcomments: The Horog-heny (265m) lies 2km ENE of the village of Köveskál, 4m N of northern shore of Lake Balaton. The fossiliferous localities occur on the forested northern slope of Horog-hegy, between the hilltop and an E-W running forest track.
stratcomments: The bulk of the hill is formed by Megyehegy Dolomite (lower Pelsonian?), overlain by gently dipping beds of Felsõörs Limestone (Pelsonian to Illyrian), about 40m in thickness.
lithdescript: Horog-hegy I: The lowermost unit is a more than 50 cm thick, light grey, slightly siliceous, unfossiliferous limestone (mudstone). This is overlain, with a sharp contact, by a 40cm thick, light brown, coarse-grained bioclastic limestone with brachiopods of rock-forming amount ("Upper Recaro")\r\nHorog-hegy II: a smaller, 2m wide outcrop around 50m eastward from the previous one, along the strike of the beds. The wxposed sequence is almost the same as in Horog-hegy I, but here the lowermost mudstone us well-bedded, slightly bituminous and yielded a poorly preserved Bulogites, and the brachiopod limestone ("Upper Recoaro") attains only 20 sm thickness.

The small mound is approximately 58 m S. 75"W. of a benchmark indicated by a pipe cemented into bedrock, northeast of the massive exposure. The main outcrop of the massive upper Capitan Limestone is approximately 15 m south of the benchmark. The small reef mass is approximately 445 m west and 475 m south of the northeast corner of section 24, T. 23 S., R. 25 E., at latitude 32'17'34" north, longitude 104'20'44" west, on the Kitchen Cove, 1985, 7.5 Minute Provisional Quadrangle. The Dark Canyon locality is approximately 6.2 km (3.9 miles) west from the junction of the Dark Canyon access road with U.S. Highway 62-180, and that junction is 7.0 km (4.4 miles) southwest of the Carlsbad Airport entrance and roadside park area. The small bioherm is about 8 m long, 5.5 m wide, and elongate toward the northwest. Smaller sample from western part of older massive reef exposure, approximately 5 m west of a small tree along the edge of the alluvial fill.

collection_name: Hiraiso Fm. in the Hiraiso Coast, Facies Ha
geogcomments: Outcrop on the Hiraiso Coast in Motoyoshi-cho, Miyagi Pref., Japan, the type locality of the Hiraiso Formation. The rocky coast between Maekawara and Akaushi fishing ports provides a continous 800m outcrop that embraces the entire Hiraiso Formation.
stratcomments: Bando (1970) originally assigned the Hiraiso Fm. to the Griesbachian, later it was assigned to the Smithian by Nakazawa et al. (1994). Reidentification of Bando's ammonite as Neocolumbites and discovery of Tirolites in the lower part of the formation suggests a Spathian age for the Hiraiso Formation (Shigeta & Nakajima, 2017). Listed fossils belong to the Facies Ha, one of nine identified facies in the Hiraiso Fm.

geology_comments: Upper inner shelf.

Assigned to the early Midian on the basis of fusulinids Minojapanella and Lantschichites (although questionably identified). The overlying Kundil Formation contains Kubergandian (Roadian) fusulinids such as Cancellina and Praesumatrina (Flugel & Gaetani, 1991), although these are considered to be reworked by Gaetani et al. (1995). The Kundil Fm also contains conodonts assigned a Murgabian age by Gaetani et al. (1995), although the smooth-platform Mesogondolella species are challenging to use for biostratigraphy. An early Midian (late Wordian) age is retained here.
collection_comments: All specimens are housed at the Museo di Paleontologia (MPUM) del Dipartimento di Scienze della Terra dell'Universtia degli Studi de Milano (Italy).

geogcomments: Shore platform below Shot Tower at Taronga.  Grid reference EN278433.
stratcomments: Late Paleozoic fosiliferous marine sequence is almost everywhere subhorizontal and has a total thickness of about 675 meters. The late Lymingtonian (?Kazanian) assemblages described range throughout the uppermost 160 meters of this sequence in the Malbina Formation Member E and the overlying Risdon Sandstone and Abels Bay Formation and correlative beds. No measured section. Assigned to the Echinalosia hanloni/robusta zone by Briggs (1998), in the basal part of the APP4.2 palynomorph zone. Laurie et al. (2016) placed the base of APP4.2 at 266.8 Ma, coincident with the base of the Wordian (266.9 Ma in Wu et al., 2020), so a Wordian age is assigned to these collections.
collection_comments: All fossils figured herein are deposited in the fossil collections of the Geological Survey of Tasmania (GST) or the Geology Department, University of Tasmania (UTGF).

geogcomments: 1 km NW of the small village Selong, Nyalam County, S Tibet (Shen et al. 2000)
stratcomments: Equivalent to Bed 17 in Shen et al. (2000). The contact between the Selong Group and the overlying Kangshare Formation is marked by the Caliche Bed, a thin layer of pedogenic calcrete which varies laterally in thickness. The Kangshare Formation is 7.0 m thick and is divided into three beds (Jin et al., 1996): Waagenites Bed, Otoceras Bed, and Ophiceras Bed. The Otoceras and Ophiceras Beds are Triassic in age.
lithdescript: Bioclasts are finer in size and form around 35%, and sometimes less than 10%, of the rock. Bioclastics are usually well sorted, ranging from 0.5 mm to 2.0 mm in diameter. Packstone with poorly sorted bioclastics is also observed where the diameter of bioclastics may be up to 20 mm with slightly abraded unbroken crinoid stems. Contains greater amounts of ostracod and gastropod shells.\r\nJA: described by Shen et al. 2000 as a brown dolomitized crinoid packstone with brachiopods, corals, bryozoans, ostracods, foraminifers and calcareous sponges, above the "Caliche Bed", 0.07 m thick
geology_comments: This bed represents lag carbonate deposits formed in shallow, medium-energy shoal and in inter-shoal depressions.

Contains greater amounts of ostracod and gastropod shells.\r\nJA: described by Shen et al. 2000 as a brown dolomitized crinoid packstone with brachiopods, corals, bryozoans, ostracods, foraminifers and calcareous sponges, above the "Caliche Bed", 0.07 m thick

geogcomments: 1 km NW of the small village Selong, Nyalam County, S Tibet (Shen et al. 2000)
stratcomments: Equivalent to Bed 17 in Shen et al. (2000). The contact between the Selong Group and the overlying Kangshare Formation is marked by the Caliche Bed, a thin layer of pedogenic calcrete which varies laterally in thickness. The Kangshare Formation is 7.0 m thick and is divided into three beds (Jin et al., 1996): Waagenites Bed, Otoceras Bed, and Ophiceras Bed. The Otoceras and Ophiceras Beds are Triassic in age.

stratcomments: The Murdock Mountain Formation is laterally equivalent to the Rex Chert Member of the Phosphoria Formation in northeastern Utah and southeastern Idaho, and to the Plympton Formation in southeastern Nevada and northwestern Utah (Wardlaw and other, 1979). Age based on conodont Merrillina galeata.
lithdescript: Fossils surrounded by bioclastic materials, pellets, micrite, and microspar; rocks classified as wackestone or packstone
geology_comments: Formation consists of 537 m of cherty siltstone, silty chert, fine-grained sandstone, and thin beds of dolomite and limestone. There are two thin fossiliferous limestone tongues occur in the uppermost part of the Murdock Mountain Formation in the Leach Mountains. Uppermost tongue is the Thamnosia beds and the underlying tongue is the Stenodiscus beds.
collection_comments: Samples of rock types and bryozoans were collected at 30 cm intervals or at each lithologic change in the Stenodiscus beds.

geogcomments: SPECIFIC LOCATION: Stream cut, right bank, Kavik River, Mt Michleson quadrangle, Alaska. LAT/LONG: Estimate stated in text.
stratcomments: STRATIGRAPHIC RELATIONS: One of three members of Ivishak Formation, including Kavik, Ledge Sandstone, and Fire Creek Siltstone. Contact with underlying Middle Permian Ikiakpaurak Mbr of the Echooka Fm is not well exposed, but is unconformable. THICKNESS: Kavik Mbr is 185 m thick at its type section. AGE: Griesbachian. Contains an ammonite and bivalve fauna of Early Triassic age. Ammonite Ophiceras commune and Claraia stachei indicate a late Griesbachian age.
lithdescript: GENERAL LITHOLOGY: Thin-bedded, laminated, silty shale and sandstone. A few thin, very fine grained, argillaceous sandstone beds occur locally within the member. LITHIFICATION: Assumed to be lithified.

collection_name: Lazurnaya Bay Fm (lower part) - South Primorye
geogcomments: GENERAL LOCATION: Exposures along eastern coast of Abrek Bay, near Krym, South Primorye, Russia. LAT/LONG: Estimate based on Fig. 1 (Zakharov and Shigeta 2000).
stratcomments: STRATIGRAPHIC RELATIONS: Lower Triassic strata in region are lithostratigraphically divided into the Lazurnaya Bay and Zhitkov Formations in an upward sequence. The Lazurnaya Bay Fm unconformably overlies the Permian Abrek Fm. THICKNESS: The Lazurnaya Bay Fm is 57.9 m thick in the Abrek Bay region. AGE: Contains an assemblage that suggest the upper Induan age, underlying lower Olenekian (lower part of the Hedenstroemia bisphorensis Zone) in the upper part of the formation. The Induan/Olenekian boundary is located at 55 m above the base of the formation.

geogcomments: SPECIFIC LOCATION: Approximately 1 mile northeast of Crittenden Springs, near Montello, Elko County, Nevada. Crittenden Springs quad map. Exposed in SW1/4 SW1/4 sect 34, T. 43 N., R. 69 E., W1/2 SW1/4 sec. 3, T. 42 N., R. 69 E.\r\nLAT/LONG: estimated based on Crittenden Springs, Nevada. NOTES: There is some confusion as to the proper name for this locality. Muller 1956, p. 82) and Clark 1957 (p. 2194) have used the name Dinner Springs canyon, and his name is apparently the one used by the people of Montello, Nevada. Kummel and Steele state, however, that is name does not appear on official maps, whereas Crittenden Springs does.
stratcomments: STRATIGRAPHIC RELATIONS: Unknown bounding lithostratigraphic units. THICKNESS: Stratigraphic section of 175 ft. AGE: Meekoceras graciliatus zone, Scythian stage. Assigned here to the Olenekian by the enterer. STRATIGRAPHIC POSITION: Collection is from "Unit a", a 17-33 ft thick limestone, presumably at the base of section (not stated). LITHOSTRATIGRAPHY: No lithostratigraphic units named in Kummel and Steele (1962). Assignment to the Thaynes Fm is based on more recent publications from the same sections, including Gardner and Mapes (2000).
lithdescript: SPECIFIC LITHOLOGY: Limestone, light gray, with limonite flecks and partings, fine to coarse crystalline, thick-bedded, weathers brown. Approximately half or more of the rock is composed of cephapholod skeletal elements. LITHIFICATION: Lithified, on the basis of observation of figured specimens.
geology_comments: ENVIRONMENT: No environmental data reported in text. According to Gardner and Mapes (2000).. "inner slope to basin facies, depths ranging from 75 to 125 m" and was assigned to a carbonate shallow subtidal environment. However, I assign a carbonate deep subtidal shelf environment based on this description. TECTONIC SETTING: No tectonic data reported in text. SEQUENCE STRATIGRAPHY: No sequence stratigraphic data reported.\r\n

collection_name: G2-zawa Valley, T7, Takakura-yama Mountain, Iwaki City
geogcomments: Takakurayama area, eastern Abukuma Mountains, i.e., Yaguki, Yotsukuramachi, Iwaki City, Fukushima Prefecture, northeast Japan
stratcomments: The Takakurayama Formation is exposed in the northeastern slope of Mt. Takakurayama, dipping 30-45 degrees W and striking in a general NNE-SSW direction, and occupying the area of about 3 square kilometers. This formation is subdivided into three members: 1) the Iriishikura Member, consisting mostly of shale with some sandstone beds, 290 m thick, 2) the Motomura Member, consisting mostly of sandstone and conglomerate with some shale beds, 167 m thick, and 3) the Kashiwadaria Member, consisting mostly of shale with some sandstone and conglomerate beds, 348 m thick, in ascending order.
lithdescript: sandy shale
geology_comments: probably derived from shallow marine continental shelf to a deep-sea basin by sediment-gravity flows
collectors: J. Tazawa, N. Kaneko, S. Hasegawa
lithdescript.1: sandy shale

geogcomments: 12 miles east of Kamloops, BC, at Campbell Siding; north side of Thompson River
stratcomments: From upper part of unit. Nassichuk (1977) assigned an "early Guadalupian (Wordian)" age. It is possible, and perhaps more likely, that this collection is Roadian - the traditional Wordian encompasses the upper part of what is now formally defined as Roadian. The ammonoid Daubichites (although tentatively identified here) is characteristically Roadian, and Paraceltites and Waagenoceras both also occur in the upper Roadian in west Texas. Nelson & Nelson (1985) identified fusulinids that are early Guadalupian, and perhaps Wordian as Dunbarula laudoni co-occurs with Yabeina in its type area elsewhere. Limestone in the Harper Ranch Group spans a long age range based on conodonts (Orchard & Foster, 1988), including abundant Sakmarian-Kungurian ages. It is not clear whether the brachiopods and ammonoids were collected from the same beds or over the same age range.
geology_comments: environmental call is tentatively based on taphonomic/lithologic data provided; may be deep subtidal, but unlikely

The Difunta sections begins where the Arroyo la Difunta debouches from the hills east of Cerro San Pedro, and is measured westward to the Puerto de Sardinas, where the basal beds are overlapped by the Cretaceous.
stratcomments: Part of middle Guadalupe
lithdescript: Dark gray-brown lava flows and graywacke alternating with about 30% dark-gray shale, and containing two lenses 1 to 3 feet thick of sponge-bearing limestone (from section description, p. 13). Upper part black shale with streaks of buff limestone, graywacke, and some interbedded lava and limestone. Lower part lava, graywacke, and shale. Beds 8 and 9 and upper part of bed 10 (From a general stratigraphy table, Fig. 3, p. 19).

collection_name: King 8, Bed 14, La Difunta section, Las Delicias
geogcomments: Near Las Delicias, in the southwestern part of the State of Coahuila. Concretionary shale in area of complicated structure south-southeast of Cerro Prieto Norte.  The Difunta sections begins where the Arroyo la Difunta debouches from the hills east of Cerro San Pedro, and is measured westward to the Puerto de Sardinas, where the basal beds are overlapped by the Cretaceous.
stratcomments: Part of middle Guadalupian (Cherry Canyon-Word) in west Texas and southeast New Mexico.
lithdescript: Shale and graywacke (from section description, p. 13). Prominent limestone layers separated from one another by shale, graywacke, and lava. Beds 11 to 17 and lower part of bed 10. Most imporant member is bed 15, which caps Cerro Caballo. Massive limestones have adundant sponges, crinoidal fragments; shales and thin limestones contain cephalopods. (From a general stratigraphy table, Fig. 3, p. 19).

geogcomments: Haushi-Huqf Area. Five sections located in a small area between 21 00'37"N-57 39'35"E and 21 02'06"N-57 41'23"E, along the northwestern flank of the Haushi uplift. The Huqf area is located on the southeastern margin of the Arabian Plate, in the Sultanate of Oman.
stratcomments: Composite section built on five sections. Khuff is part of an unconformable second mega-sequence, which consists of the fluvial terrigenous Gharif Fm., overlain by marine marls and bioclastic limestones of the Khuff Fm.
lithdescript: cross-bedded, pebbly, bioclastic quartzarenites
geology_comments: This member is divided into two subunits. The lower subunit consists of cross-bedded, pebbly, bioclastic quartzarenites, and the overlying upper subunit consists of thin-bedded, cross-bedded, coarse to medium quartarenites alternating with bioclastic limestone. The lower subunit is interpreted as a barrier beach complex, and the upper subunit is interpreted as a mixed sand-mud shoreface environment.

collection_name: Muddy Mountains Overton locality - Placunopsis bioherm
lithdescript:
Placunopsis bioherms. Nine individual bivalve mounds occur in a single bed across 100 m of lateral exposure.The internal structure of all the bioherms consists of small, irregularly stacked Placunopsis valves (1–10 mm in length, 1 mm thick) that appear in the field as stacked millimeter-size elongate clasts. The Placunopsis bioherms broadly resemble stromatolites (Bachmann, 1979) due
to their hemispheroidal, columnar, and laminated macrostructures. The
small size and irregular shape of the shells also makes it difficult to
recognize them as bivalves in the field.
ecospace_comments: Aragonite prevalent\r\nFrom: Pruss et al. (2007): The outer layer of a bivalve shell, or ostracum, is composed of foliated calcite, which represents the original structure of the shell. The inner shell layer, or hypostracum, which was originally secreted as aragonite (Carter, 1990), now consists of sparry calcite or silica that replaced the aragonite.

lithdescript: 'The Early and Middle Triassic ammonoids occur in great abundance in very fine-grained limestone, mostly red, but in part grey or green. The colour, nature of the matrix, and abundance of ammonoids is the facies of the Hallstatt limestone.'
geology_comments: 'The Hallstatt facies is generally interpreted as a pelagic deposit laid down far from any source of terrigenous sediment. Close juxtaposition of ammonoid zones is the general rule and indicates very low rates of sedimentation. The depth at which Hallstatt rocks formed has long been debated. A summary of views up to about 1970 is given in Tozer (1971). In that account a deep water environment was suggested but the arguments favouring deposition at about 200 m, as on seamounts, seem to be strongest (e.g. Jenkyns 1970).'

collection_name: Ridge north of Wadi Alwa, Wadi Alwa I, collection 118C
geogcomments: This locality is about 50 km south of Muscat (sheet NF-40-039 Wadi Tayin, 1:100 000). Wadi Alwa I. This, the largest mass of Triassic rock, is near the summit of the ridge.
stratcomments: Wadi Alwa I. The maximum dimension is at least 100 m. It is tabular preserving about 25 m of strata, mostly red limestone. The strata dip easterly at a low\r\nangle. Beds form a small bluff where a sequence of three ammonoid beds (ll8A,B,C) was determined in a stratigraphic thickness of about 25 m. Collection 118C. Lower Anisian.
lithdescript: 'red rocks, but different from the Hallstatt-type limestones, being nodular and of a marly nature.'
geology_comments: 'From a lithofacies standpoint these rocks are more comparable with the 'Ammonitico Rosso'. lithdescript:
Reef builders: Frame-building and baffling
organisms: hypercalcified sphinctozoan and inozoan sponges, sclerosponges, stromatoporoid sponge, bryozoans, and hydrozoans.
Binding organisms: Archaeolithoporella, Palaeoaplysina, Tubiphytes, and cyanobacteria.

reef dwellers:
Echinoderms, ammonites, bivalves, brachiopods, gastropods, benthic foraminifera, calcareous algae, and single rugose corals.

Rock type and reef-related depositional characteristic:
Fore-reef slope: spiculitic-calcispherical cherty wackestone with reef breccias Reef core: sponge framestone and bafflestone, Archaeolithoporella and cyanobacteria bindstone, and sponge framestone with the encrusting Archaeolithoporella
Reef flat (reef crest): packstone with reef breccia
Reef base: echinodermal packstone to grainstone
Back-reef lagoon: bioclastic packstone with calcareous algae, gastropods, and foraminifers.

Reef type:
Metazoan reef at the shallow carbonate platform margin

geogcomments: 12 miles east of Kamloops, BC, at Campbell Siding; north side of Thompson River
stratcomments: From upper part of unit. Nassichuk (1977) assigned an "early Guadalupian (Wordian)" age. It is possible, and perhaps more likely, that this collection is Roadian - the traditional Wordian encompasses the upper part of what is now formally defined as Roadian. The ammonoid Daubichites (although tentatively identified here) is characteristically Roadian, and Paraceltites and Waagenoceras both also occur in the upper Roadian in west Texas. Nelson & Nelson (1985) identified fusulinids that are early Guadalupian, and perhaps Wordian as Dunbarula laudoni co-occurs with Yabeina in its type area elsewhere. Limestone in the Harper Ranch Group spans a long age range based on conodonts (Orchard & Foster, 1988), including abundant Sakmarian-Kungurian ages. It is not clear whether the brachiopods and ammonoids were collected from the same beds or over the same age range.
geology_comments: environmental call is tentatively based on taphonomic/lithologic data provided; may be deep subtidal, but unlikely

The Ferntree Fm is the youngest marine Permian unit in Tasmanian, of late Lymingtonian age. Briggs (1998) correlated the late Lymingtonian with his mainland brachiopod zones, ranging from the Echinalosia wassi zone to the Echinalosia deari zone and with palynological zones APP4.3 and APP5. Radiometric calibration of these palynologyical zones by Laurie et al. (2016) suggests that APP4.3 is mid-Wuchiapingian and APP5 spans the late Wuchiapingian and Changhsingian. A Wuchiapingian age is assigned to the Ferntree Formation here.

stratcomments: Near top of Wandrawandian Siltstone or base of Nowra Sandstone. Upper parts of the Wandrawandian Formation assigned to the Echinalosia discinia zone by Briggs (1998), although some Wandrawandian collections include brachiopods from the Echinalosia robusta/hanloni zone (the zone represented in the Nowra Formation). The upper E. discinia zone is correlated with the top of APP4.1 palynomorph zone, and the Echinalosia robusta/hanloni zone is correlated with APP4.2 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). Strata in Western Australia assigned to APP4.1 yielded U-Pb ages of 269.25 Ma or younger, indicating a late Roadian age. The APP4.2 zone was constrained as late Wordian to mid-Wuchiapingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). The E. robusta/hanloni zones are the basal part of APP4.2, so a Wordian age is assigned here.

Radiometric calibration of these palynologyical zones by Laurie et al. (2016) suggests that APP4.3 is mid-Wuchiapingian and APP5 spans the late Wuchiapingian and Changhsingian. A Wuchiapingian age is assigned to the Ferntree Formation here.

geogcomments: Selby's Rock is now on display on the property of the Kangaroo Valley museum, but originally from hill slope north of Broger's Creek, approximately 7 km east of Kangaroo Valley (property of Mr. J. Walker), N.S,W., that section where sands and silts of the Berry Formation interdigitate with volcanoclastic sediments of the Gerringong Volcanics.
stratcomments: Assigned to APP4.2 (Echinalosia runnegari-E. wassi brachiopod zones) by Briggs (1998). According to the radiometric calibrations of Laurie et al. The overlying Broughton Formation yielded an early Capitanian radiometric age of 263.51 Ma in its upper part (Metcalf et al., 2015), so a late Wordian age is assigned to the Berry Formation here.

geogcomments: "Punkt 902" is a site near Serpiano, about 1 km WSW of the peak of Monte San Giorgio.
stratcomments: The Besano Formation is also known as "Grenzbitumenzone" or "Scisti bituminosi". It comprises strata from the uppermost Anisian to the lowermost Ladinian.
lithdescript: "The Grenzbitumenzone [GBZ] of the Tessiner Kalkalpen is an alternation of dolomite beds of various thickness (3 up to 50 cm), numerous, thinner layers of finely laminated, black bituminous shales (Schwarzschiefer), and few, up to several centimeters thick, volcaniclastic interbeds (volcanic ashes). At the excavation site P.902 near Mirigioli at Monte San Giorgio, the total tickness of the GBZ, comprising the beds 3 to 186 at this location, was measured to be 15.8 m. The beds of the more or less laminated dolomites make up about 80% of the total thickness of the GBZ. Depending on the degree of weathering and on the content of organic matter (up to 12 weight %), the dolomite beds are dark grey, dark brown to light beige. In freshly-mined condition, in the galleries of the former mines, they are almost black (high organic matter content) or dark to medium grey. The the original carbonate mud is completely dolomitized. There is no evidence of other carbonate phases. The laminae of the mostly parallel and continuous fine lamination vary in thickness from 0.1 to 5 mm. In most cases the lamination is caused by a rhythmic change of the content of dolomite, clay minerals, and organic matter. However, in dolomite-rich laminae also graded bedding may be observed occasionally. [...] The black shales contain no or at most few carbonate. The content of organic matter ranges from 10 up to 40 weight %. The fine lamination of freshly-mined shale is well visible only in thin sections. Partly weathered, the black shale delaminates into thin (mostly less than 1 mm) laminae [...]. The lamination is caused by a change of organic matter, clay minerals, and quartz. The quartz is mainly biogenic. Radiolarians are very common and partly form small laminae of silica in the black shales." (translated from H.-P. Rieber, 2000, in D. Meischner (ed.) Europäische Fossillagerstätten, German edition)
geology_comments: "The GBZ was deposited within a largely closed marine basin with restricted water circulation (Zorn 1971, Rieber et Sorbini 1983, Bernasconi, 1994). The basin was enclosed by carbonate platforms. The fine-grained sediments and missing evidence of reworking, the mostly complete preserved vertebrate skeletons which are not oriented indicate that there was at most a weak current at the bottom of the basin and that the sediments were deposited below wave base. The water depth of the basin is estimated to have been 30 to 100 m with a gradual deepening through time. The undisturbed lamination of the GBZ rocks and a lack of autochthonous benthos point out that the basin in which the GBZ generated had a stable stratification of the water column and that the bottom water was almost always anoxic and rich in H2S. The common remains of highly marine animals, primarily pelagic fish, ichthyosaurs, ammonoids, and daonellids prove that the surface waters had normnal salinity and was at least periodically connected to the waters of the Triassic Paleotethys." (translated from Rieber, 2000)\r\nSequence Stratigraphy: looks and sounds like the maximum flooding interval of a transgressive systems tract
preservation_comments: "Isolated bones of larger reptiles or fishes are less abundant than whole skeletons. The abundance of the vertebrates, occurring in both black shales and dolomite, varies between the beds. All in all vertebrate remains are more common in the black shales than in the dolomite beds. [...] The preservation of the skeletons, apart from compression by compaction, is generally very good. Finest details of bone surfaces and scales are preserved [...] " (translated from H.-P. Rieber, 2000, in D. Meischner (ed.) Europäische Fossillagerstätten, German edition)

stratcomments: 500 feet below top of Middle Bowen Marine Series, from the upper part of the Blenheim Subgroup (Dickins 1989). This part of the Blenheim Formation is Wuchiapingian in age, containing brachiopod zones correlated with the upper part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone or - more likely for this collection - lower part of APP5 (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age and APP5 as mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). However, overlying units in the Fort Cooper Coal Measures yield latest Wuchiapingian U-Pb ages (Phillips et al., 2018), constraining the upper Blenheim Fm to Wuchiapingian.

stratcomments: From the upper part of the stratigraphy containing the Big Strophalosia zone and clarkei bed. Upper part of the Blenheim Formation correlated with the upper part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone or lower part of APP5 (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age and APP5 as mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). However, overlying units in the Fort Cooper Coal Measures yield latest Wuchiapingian U-Pb ages (Phillips et al., 2018), constraining the upper Blenheim Fm to Wuchiapingian.

stratcomments: Presence of Pseudostrophalosia clarkei suggests an age within the P. clarkei zone, correlated with the lower part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016).

According to the stratigraphic column in Dickins et al. (1964), MC293 is from near the top of the Blenheim Formation, in "Fauna IV" of Dickins et al. and well above the Big Strophalosia Zone. The Big Strophalosia Zone contains the Pseudostrophalosia clarkei zone of Briggs (1998), correlated with the top of APP4.3 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). Therefore, this locality is likely at a higher level, probably within APP5 palynomorph zone. The APP5 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). However, overlying units in the Fort Cooper Coal Measures yield latest Wuchiapingian U-Pb ages (Phillips et al., 2018), constraining the upper Blenheim Fm to Wuchiapingian.

stratcomments: Formerly Gerringong Volcanics. A sample 2 m below the top of the formation yielded a radiometric date of 263.51 Ma, within the basal Capitanian (Metcalf et al., 2015), but nearly all fossils come from the basal Westley Park Sandstone or Kiama Sandstone members. Therefore, a Wordian age is assigned.

Correlative with the Berry and Broughton Formations, and assigned to the Echinalosia runnegari and E. wassi brachiopod zones by Briggs (1998), and to the APP4.2 palynomorph zone. The APP4.2 zone has its inferred base (266.8 Ma, according to calibrations in Laurie et al., 2016) nearly coincident with the base of the Wordian (266.9 in Wu et al., 2020), and ranges to the early Wuchiapingian. A sample 2 m below the top of the Broughton Formation yielded a radiometric date of 263.51 Ma, within the basal Capitanian (Metcalf et al., 2015), so the a Wordian age is assigned.

stratcomments: Limestone in the Harper Ranch Group spans a long age range based on conodonts (Orchard & Foster, 1988), including abundant Sakmarian-Kungurian ages. Assigned to the Black Jack Formation (now considered a group), from a shallow marine facies underlying the Arkarula Sandstone member. In the Santos Brawboy 1 well, the Pamboola Formation underlies the Arkarula Fm, so the collection is assigned to the Pamboola Fm. In that well, the Pamboola Formation belongs to APP4.2-4.3 palynomorph zone, and is older than 257.33 Ma and younger than 262.54 Ma (Laurie et al., 2016). In the Santos Slacksmith 1 well, the Pamboola Fm is older than 258.05 Ma and younger than 264.75 Ma. Presence of Echinalosia denisoni suggests an age within the P. clarkei zone, correlated with the lower part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016).

collection_name: Huai Mae Phlung, Doi Pha Phlung 20F, Lampang Province
geogcomments: Location stated as 99.60' W, 18 degrees 80'N. Map in Ishibashi et al. shows position more accurately.  North and east of Chiangmai, on or near the Lampang-Ngao road, south of Ngao.  Equivalent to locality 1 in Ishibashi et al., 1994.  They state that it is also equivalent to locality 88080703 in Kobayashi and Sakagami, 1989 but the K and S description suggests that their locality 88080601 (in the river at Huai Mae Phlung) fits better.
stratcomments: Huai Tak Formation is uppermost of Ngao Group, overlain by latest Permian volcanics and Triassic Lampang Group.
preservation_comments: Moderately well preserved, chiefly as natural moulds, but are deformed and so crowded together that it is impossible to avoid some breakage in extracting specimens. A number of species are represented by fragments.
taxonomy_comments: Only includes brachiopods. Fusilinids and conodonts are absent, as are corals, gastropods, and bryozoans. A number of pteriiform and myalinid bivalves and rare ammonoid impressions are present.

stratcomments: Black Alley shale contains ash beds dated at 254.41 (base of unit), 254.32 Ma (middle of unit) and 254.08 Ma (top boundary of unit), according to Metcalfe et al. (2015) and Phillips et al. (2018). In addition, the unit was correlated with the Echinalosia voiseyi brachiopod zone and middle of the APP5 palynomorph zone by Briggs (1998). The APP5 zone was calibrated as mid-Wuchiapingian to Changhsingian in Laurie et al. (2016). This evidence indicates a latest Wuchiapingian age for the Black Alley shale, with the uppermost part possibly being early Changhsingian (using 254.14 Ma as the Wuchiapingian-Changhsingian boundary).

collection_name: Levyy Titan Creek, Bed 42, Intomodesma costatum Subzone, Okhotsk Massif
lithdescript: Alternating beds (5–10 m) of light greenish gray fine to medium-grained compact massive sandstones and packets of intercalated thin-bedded light greenish gray fine-grained sandstones and greenish gray todark gray, sometimes, carbonaceous–\r\nclayey siltstones with laminae (from 1 mm to 1–3 cm) of black shales. The section encloses rare interbeds of fine- to medium-grained poorly sorted clayey sandstones and ellipsoid calcareous concretions 5 × 10 cm in size. There are\r\nalso rare interbeds (5–10 cm) of small- to medium-pebbled conglomerates at the top of the member and 55 m below the latter.

collection_name: UQ L4577, quarry along highway north of Theodore, Bowen Basin
stratcomments: Assigned the Echinalosia ovalis zone of Briggs (1998) and the middle part of palynomorph zone APP5. Laurie et al. (2016) calibrated the APP5 zone to mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian. Phillips et al. (2018) marked the Platypus Tuff bed (dated as 256.01 Ma in Metcalf et al., 2015) within the Flat Top Formation but suggested that the top of the formation was 255.13 Ma based on correlation with a tuff bed at the top of the Colinlea Sandstone equivalent. These constraints suggest a Wuchiapingian age for the Flat Top Formation.

geogcomments: east side of Slaty Creek, 400 yards at 35' east of north from the Sandy Hill to Drake road crossing of Slaty Creek. 356 E 173N.
stratcomments: The unit was assigned to the Echinalosia voiseyi brachiopod zone and middle of the APP5 palynomorph zone by Briggs (1998). The APP5 zone was calibrated as mid-Wuchiapingian to Changhsingian in Laurie et al. (2016). A Changhsingian age is possible, but a Wuchiapingian age is assigned on the basis of the youngest marine deposits elsewhere in eastern Australia.

geogcomments: Hill slope on northern side of Slaty Ck at about 1737 m at 030° from the Sandy Hill to Drake road crossing of Slaty Ck (Drake 1 mile Mil. Map 363 186).
stratcomments: Assigned to Gilgurry Mudstone but brachiopods suggest older Cataract River Member. Brachiopods suggest the Echinalosia hanloni zone, correlated with APP4.2 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.2 zone was constrained as late Wordian to mid-Wuchiapingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). The E. hanloni zone is the basal part of APP4.2, so a Wordian age is assigned here.

Bando (1970) originally considered the age of the Hiraiso Formation to be Griesbachian (early Induan) based on a single ammonoid identified as Glyptophiceras cf. gracile from a floated block of siltstone, which possibly came from the Osawa Formation (Ehiro, 2002). Later, Nakazawa et al. (1994) attributed the specimen to G. aequicostatus and assigned it a late Smithian age. However, our examination of the specimen indicates that it is not G. aequicostatus, and instead should be assigned to the early Spathian ammonoid Neocolumbites Zakharov.

collection_name: Eddystone 1 well, interval C, 798.1-798.2 m depth
lithdescript: Between 797.55 m and 805.1 m is a structureless, pebbly, sandy mudstone. Pebbles and sand grains are randomly distributed, except for a slight decrease in pebble abundance in the top 2.5 m. Pebbles include a few examples with maximum diameters between 50 mm and 120 mm. Bioturbation is present throughout, and fragmentary fossils, ranging in size from less than 1 mm to almost complete brachiopods 30 mm in diameter, are scattered throughout or concentrated in\r\ndiffuse bands.

collection_name: Eddystone 1 well, interval E, 674.9-675.2 m depth (GSQ L2117)
stratcomments: Assigned to Pseudostrophalosia crassa--Echinalosia deari brachiopod zones and lower APP5 palynomorph zone by Briggs (1998). APP5 palynomorph zone ranges from mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian based on radiometric constraints (Laurie et al., 2016), but this formation constrained to the Wuchiapingian by radiometric dates in the Black Alley shale of 254.32 Ma and 254.08 Ma (Metcalfe et al., 2015) and Phillips et al., 2018).
geology_comments: Sediments derived from adjacent fan deltas during periods of major flooding

geogcomments: On a branch of Barfield-Banana road. 10.4 km from Banana area. 6.4 km N of Mount Flat Top; Pors. 3 and 5 boundary, Parish Neiman, Co Ferguson. MONTO[yd] 315 950\r\n(Monto 4 mile 315 949).
stratcomments: Assigned the Echinalosia ovalis zone of Briggs (1998) and the middle part of palynomorph zone APP5. Laurie et al. (2016) calibrated the APP5 zone to mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian. Phillips et al. (2018) marked the Platypus Tuff bed (dated as 256.01 Ma in Metcalf et al., 2015) within the Flat Top Formation but suggested that the top of the formation was 255.13 Ma based on correlation with a tuff bed at the top of the Colinlea Sandstone equivalent. These constraints suggest a Wuchiapingian age for the Flat Top Formation.

geogcomments: 1.6 km S of Banana·Barfield road, 8.8 km from Banana, Par. 8. Par. Nieman. Co. Ferguson. MONTO[yd] 312 957.

A Wuchiapingian age is assigned to the Barfield Formation here.

stratcomments: Horizon B. About 45 m below the top of the group.\r\nThe Ferntree Fm is the youngest marine Permian unit in Tasmanian, of late Lymingtonian age. Briggs (1998) correlated the late Lymingtonian with his mainland brachiopod zones, ranging from the Echinalosia wassi zone to the Echinalosia deari zone and with palynological zones APP4.3 and APP5. Radiometric calibration of these palynologyical zones by Laurie et al. (2016) suggests that APP4.3 is mid-Wuchiapingian and APP5 spans the late Wuchiapingian and Changhsingian. A Wuchiapingian age is assigned to the Ferntree Formation here.

(2016), APP4.2 spans the latest Wordian through early Wuchiapingian. stratcomments: Correlative with the Berry and Broughton Formations, and assigned to the Echinalosia runnegari and E. wassi brachiopod zones by Briggs (1998), and to the APP4.2 palynomorph zone. The APP4.2 zone has its inferred base (266.8 Ma, according to calibrations in Laurie et al., 2016) nearly coincident with the base of the Wordian (266.9 in Wu et al., 2020), and ranges to the early Wuchiapingian. A sample 2 m below the top of the Broughton Formation yielded a radiometric date of 263.51 Ma, within the basal Capitanian (Metcalf et al., 2015), so the a Wordian age is assigned.

stratcomments: Presence of Pseudostrophalosia crassa suggests an age within the P. crassa zone, correlated with the middle part of APP5 palynomorph zone (Briggs, 1998). The APP5 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). However, overlying units in the Fort Cooper Coal Measures yield latest Wuchiapingian U-Pb ages (Phillips et al., 2018), constraining the upper Blenheim Fm to Wuchiapingian.

geogcomments: Section measured from Yinshangpo to Sizishan, in the vicinity of Qingyan, a small town 25 km S of Guiyang, the capital of Guizhou Province.
stratcomments: Bed 4 (units KC 259-262) is 80 m thick. About 200 m above base of Qingyan Formation.
lithdescript: Qingyan Formation consists mainly of gray to yellowish-green noncalcareous shale, pale-to dark-gray marl, calcareous shale, and argillaceous limestone, usually thin-bedded. Most of the fossils are collected from the shale and marl.
geology_comments: Evaporative basin in Sichuan and north Guizhou separated from open marine to south in Yunnan and Guangxi by biohermal belt, located just north of Qingyan. The area near Qingyan was a prebiohermal facies. (Apparently fore-reef or something equivalent, located on the slope?)

geogcomments: Access to four of the sections (South Sage, A, B, and D; and East Sage) is gained by traveling west from Afton for approximately 4 km (2.5 mi), turn south and follow the main road to Fairview, Wyoming (about 3.2 km). From Fairview, follow Crow Creek Road southwesterly for approximately 16 km (10 mi) to the Sage Creek-Crow Creek confluence. Travel northward along the dirt road which parallels Sage Creek for about 3.2 km (2 mi) where the road forks. Follow the left fork into South Sage Creek canyon for about 1 km (0.6 mi). The East Sage section is located about 2.4 km (1.5 mi) north of South Sage A. It is reached by following the right fork of the dirt road to Sage Creek. This section is located on the north side of the drainage in the SE 1/4 SE 1/4 sec. 1, T. 9 S., R. 45 E.
stratcomments: Davydov et al. 2017 dated an ash bed in the upper Meade Peak Member at 260.57 ± 0.07 / 0.14 / 0.31 Ma, indicating that the Meade Peak is as young as uppermost Capitanian.
lithdescript: Limestone tongue within Rex Chert
lithdescript.1: Limestone tongue within Rex Chert

geogcomments: East flank of Murdock Mountain, north center of Sec. 36, T. 39 N., R. 67 E., Loray 7 1/2-minute quadrangle, Leach Mountains, Elko County, Nevada
stratcomments: The Murdock Mountain Formation is laterally equivalent to the Rex Chert Member of the Phosphoria Formation in northeastern Utah and southeastern Idaho, and to the Plympton Formation in southeastern Nevada and northwestern Utah (Wardlaw and other, 1979). Age based on conodont Merrillina galeata.
lithdescript: Fossils surrounded by bioclastic materials, pellets, micrite, and microspar; rocks classified as wackestone or packstone
geology_comments: Formation consists of 537 m of cherty siltstone, silty chert, fine-grained sandstone, and thin beds of dolomite and limestone. There are two thin fossiliferous limestone tongues occur in the uppermost part of the Murdock Mountain Formation in the Leach Mountains. Uppermost tongue is the Thamnosia beds and the underlying tongue is the Stenodiscus beds.
collection_comments: Samples of rock types and bryozoans were collected at 30 cm intervals or at each lithologic change in the Stenodiscus beds.

geogcomments: Exposed in a moderately sharp, faulted syncline along the northeastern side of the Confusion Range, north of Cowboy Pass and old U.S. Highway 6.  1400 feet north and 400 feet west of the southeast corner of section 12, T17S, R14W on the Cowboy Pass 7 1/2 minute quadrangle.  In low hills in the northern part of the Triassic outcrops.  The locality is on the west side of a low pass, in exposures 15-30 m west of the road, northwest of where the access road bends sharply northward after passing close to a steep, narrow ledgy exposure at the gully crossing in the second L-shaped bend of the road north from the main Cowboy Pass road.
stratcomments: Approximately 260 m above base of Thaynes Formation.  Conodont zones 5 and 6 (of Carr and Paul, 1983).  Ammonoids characteristic of the Columbites-Tirolites Zone or possibly of the Prohungarites-Subcolumbites beds above.  Occur in greenish shales above and below a sandstone bed cut by transverse faults.
lithdescript: Greenish gray, calcareous shale
geology_comments: Lower part of the outer shelf facies, immediately above the tongue of red bed facies in rocks of the minor lower Spathian transgression.
preservation_comments: Platelike sponge fragments occur principally below the sandy bed, and the round stemlike parts of the goblet-shaped sponges occur in the greenish marine beds above the sandstone.

stratcomments: The Takakurayama Formation is exposed in the northeastern slope of Mt. Takakurayama, dipping 30-45 degrees W and striking in a general NNE-SSW direction, and occupying the area of about 3 square kilometers. This formation is subdivided into three members: 1) the Iriishikura Member, consisting mostly of shale with some sandstone beds, 290 m thick, 2) the Motomura Member, consisting mostly of sandstone and conglomerate with some shale beds, 167 m thick, and 3) the Kashiwadaria Member, consisting mostly of shale with some sandstone and conglomerate beds, 348 m thick, in ascending order.

geogcomments: Takakurayama area, eastern Abukuma Mountains, i.e., Yaguki, Yotsukuramachi, Iwaki City, Fukushima Prefecture, northeast Japan
stratcomments: The Takakurayama Formation is exposed in the northeastern slope of Mt. Takakurayama, dipping 30-45 degrees W and striking in a general NNE-SSW direction, and occupying the area of about 3 square kilometers. This formation is subdivided into three members: 1) the Iriishikura Member, consisting mostly of shale with some sandstone beds, 290 m thick, 2) the Motomura Member, consisting mostly of sandstone and conglomerate with some shale beds, 167 m thick, and 3) the Kashiwadaria Member, consisting mostly of shale with some sandstone and conglomerate beds, 348 m thick, in ascending order.
lithdescript: sandy shale
geology_comments: probably derived from shallow marine continental shelf to a deep-sea basin by sediment-gravity flows

The possible P/Tr mass extinction horizon is calibrated to the base of Bed 19 by the first occurrence of the conodont N. meishanensis
geology_comments: shallow, open, platform setting
preservation_comments: Preservation is variable; brachiopod specimens comprise shells, whereas both ammonoids and bivalves are moulds and crinoids are represented by inarticulated stems, bryozoans by fragmented branches, and fossil fishes by fragmented scales.
collection_comments: recovered from the surfaces of mudstone or marlstone or limestone slabs, forming total areas of 0.2 to 0.3 m2 for each sample. all of bryozoans, crinoids and fishes are excluded from quantitative analysis.

geogcomments: Collinsville 1:100 000 sheet, 881977.  West bank of Rosella Creek, 1 km south of Collinsvolle-Mount Coolon road crossing.
stratcomments: Other collections from Rosella Creek come from the Streptorhynchus pelicanensis zone, which is near the top of the formation. Upper Blenheim is likely equivalent to the Pseudostrophalosia ingelarensis zone (or possibly also P. clarkei zone) of Briggs (1998). These zones are correlated with the upper part of APP4.3 palynomorph zone or lower part of APP5 (Briggs, 1998). The APP4.3 zone was constrained as mid-Wuchiapingian age and APP5 as mid-Wuchiapingian through Changhsingian age by U-Pb dating in Laurie et al. (2016). However, overlying units in the Fort Cooper Coal Measures yield latest Wuchiapingian U-Pb ages (Phillips et al., 2018), constraining the upper Blenheim Fm to Wuchiapingian.

At or near USGS 7663.  Includes small specimen found as float 150 m north of locality.
stratcomments: A meter-thick sequence of finely laminated turbiditic wackestones approximately\r\n13 m above the base of the member. These turbidite deposits occur immediately below and between two zones of limestone lenses that are spaced about one meter apart and that contain numerous, large, silicified scaphopods referable to Plagioglypta, in addition to an unusual suite of silicified sponges. The hexactinellid sponge was collected from 0.3 m below the lowest zone of scaphopod lenses and 0.7 m above a distinctive stratigraphic unit, about 3.7 mm thick, which is bounded above and below by a pair of coarse-grained packstone\r\ndebris flows that range from 0.3 to 1.35 m thick. The fusulinid Paraboultonia splendens Skinner and Wilde, 1954, a biostratigraphic zonal indicator, occurs in these packstones and in finer grainstones, below and above the level where this hexactinellid sponge was found.
lithdescript: Finely laminated turbiditic wckestone
geology_comments: The USB probably represents a small localized debris flow that originated at the shelf margin and terminated a short distance into the basin.
